title: Research
text: I conducted a systematic RNA-seq meta-analysis of common bean stress transcriptomes (19 public datasets), combining statistical meta-analysis with machine learning and network-based gene discovery to identify consensus stress-responsive genes. I then evaluated whether SNP subsets prioritized by proximity to these evidence genes improve genomic prediction accuracy relative to standard equal-weight GBLUP and random-marker controls. This framework has been applied to bacterial wilt and soybean cyst nematode resistance in common bean, and, through cross-species ortholog mapping, to abiotic stress tolerance (drought, salt) in cowpea.

My graduate and industry work in plant pathology focused directly on disease-resistance breeding: breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, including genetic characterization of resistance loci and race-specific resistance across worldwide germplasm, and three years evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for pathogen resistance within Syngenta’s Trait Assessment pipeline.

title: Research
section: Multi-breed genomic prediction in beef cattle
text:
Multi-breed genomic prediction in beef cattle
I built and validated a full genomic prediction pipeline for puberty and fertility traits (reproductive tract score, pelvic height and width, days open, heifer pregnancy) across five beef cattle breed populations: Angus, Red Angus, Hereford, a Bos indicus-influenced population, and a pooled MultiBreed population of over 9,000 animals genotyped on an 800K SNP panel. The pipeline covers univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait single-step GBLUP and GBLUP models via BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+, with genetic parameter estimation (heritability, genetic correlations) via REML/AI-REML and prediction accuracy validated using a Linear Regression (LR) temporal validation framework. Related work includes a Breed-As-Trait analysis estimating genetic correlations for the same traits across breeds, and a population-stratification-adjusted (PCA-corrected) extension of the MultiBreed models.

title: Dotun Olaoye
text:
I hold a Bachelor of Agriculture (Honors: Crop Protection/Pathology) from the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Nigeria, and a Master of Science in Plant Breeding, Genetics and Pathology from the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, where I worked on breeding spinach for resistance to the downy mildew pathogen Peronospora effusa, including genetic characterization of resistance loci and race-specific resistance across worldwide germplasm. During this period I also conceived the RNA-seq meta-analysis and cross-species genomic prediction framework I have continued to develop since, which uses machine learning and network analysis to identify stress-responsive genes in common bean and tests whether SNP subsets prioritized by these genes improve genomic prediction accuracy for disease-resistance traits in common bean and abiotic-stress traits in cowpea.
Between the master’s and my current PhD, I spent three years as a Pathology Research Specialist at Syngenta Seeds Inc., evaluating field corn, sweet corn, and soybean for resistance to economically important plant pathogens within a commercial trait-advancement pipeline.
I am a PhD student in Statistical Genetics at the University of Missouri, Columbia, working with Dr. Jared Decker in the Genetics Area Program. My current research centers on multi-breed genomic evaluation of puberty and fertility traits in beef cattle, using single-step GBLUP and GBLUP models.
My work applies statistical genetics methods, including mixed-model genetic evaluation and Linear Regression (LR) validation, to problems in both livestock and crop improvement, building on a background in plant pathology and disease-resistance breeding.
